title: Random forests on clinical, imaging and omics data predict multiple sclerosis disability
summary: Random forest models were developed in 322 MS patients and 98 controls from four centers (clinical, MRI, OCT, genotype, cytomic and phosphoproteomic data) to predict disability accumulation, NEDA and therapy escalation. Accuracy was intermediate to high in an independent prospective cohort of 271 patients. Clinical data alone or with imaging often sufficed, and omics added slightly in some cases.
